text:
devon: Hey team, customer can't finish GitHub/Google SSO from our app. Intermittent 'state mismatch' on callback. Happens ~30% of attempts.
evelyn: Can you paste the full callback URL they see?
devon: Here's redacted: `https://app.customer/callback?code=4/0AY0e-g&state=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1Ni1fMTIz` — but our server log shows the state we received is `eyJhbGc%252D1Ni1fMTIz` (notice %252D).
sam: %252D = double-encoded '-' (percent sign encoded). Means it was encoded twice before reaching us. Any proxy/CDN in front?
devon: They use internal tracking service that inserts `utm_source=partner` at redirect. It's done by a lightweight rewrite service at their edge.
jeff (via oauth-bot): automated note: recent edge rewrite change rolled out yesterday that URL-encodes query params when appending extras.
evelyn: That would double-encode the already-encoded `state` we base64url encode. Our callback does a strict equality check between stored session state and incoming state. Double-encoding breaks it.
devon: Repro steps I used: 1) start oauth from incognito 2) complete consent 3) callback fails 1/3 times. Non-incognito sometimes works.
sam: Hypothesis: on some flows the redirect goes through their rewrite and double-encodes; other times it goes direct to us (load-balancer route) and it's fine.
julian: Quick patch idea: normalize incoming state by applying one URL-decode pass before comparing, but be careful to not accept arbitrary modifications (security).
evelyn: Agreed. We can try tolerant compare: decode once and compare both decoded and raw variants. Also log when normalization triggered.
sam: Also the PKCE code_verifier step — any failures there? The customer reported a separate 'invalid_grant' earlier but we couldn't repro.
devon: The invalid_grant looks correlated — when state mismatch happens we don't have session keyed properly so verifier missing and we see `invalid_grant`.
julian: So primary fix: handle double-encoded state. Secondary: recommend customer change edge rewrite to append utm params without re-encoding, or strip utm on redirect to our callback.
evelyn: I'll open an infra ticket to add a normalization shim in the callback handler and feature-flag it for 48 hours for this customer.
sam: Can you drop the shim behind a feature flag and add an audit log: `state_normalized=true` with the two string variants (redacted)?
julian: Pseudo patch:
```js
// in callback handler
const rawState = req.query.state || ''
let normalizedState = rawState
try {
  const once = decodeURIComponent(rawState)
  if (once !== rawState) normalizedState = once
} catch(e) { /* ignore */ }
// compare normalizedState to session.state
```
evelyn: Also escalate to SRE to contact the partner and ask them to stop percent-encoding querystring when appending tracking params.
devon: Customer ok with temporary workaround. They prefer partner side fix.
sam: Tests to add: simulate callback with single-encoded, double-encoded, and mangled states. Make sure we don't accept completely different values.
evelyn: I'll create support ticket for the customer with repro steps and timeline.
devon: Thanks. One more ask — can we surface clearer error UI to users? Right now they see 'Something went wrong'. If state mismatch we can show 'SSO redirect failed — try again or contact support' so they can retry.
julian: Agreed, small frontend tweak.
evelyn: Action items:
- julian: patch shim + tests + flag (ETA today EOD)
- sam: add audit logging + release gate (ETA tomorrow AM)
- evelyn: contact customer + partner and file support ticket (ETA 1h)
- devon: collect one full failing callback URL from customer (ETA now)
devon: sending full failing URL in DM.
evelyn: marking as high priority. :eyes:
oauth-bot: deploy note: canary rollout requested for `callback-err-fix` to 5% of traffic.
sam: will coordinate canary after code review.
julian: I'll include config to opt-out normalization per customer if they want strict mode.
evelyn: closing loop once partner confirms config change. :pray:
